reviewer.independence_note: Only 2 model families available (Claude + GPT-5.x). Reviewer is Claude Opus 5, differing from the coder (GPT-5.4) but sharing a family with the tester (Claude Sonnet). Family-level correlation with the tester is a known limitation of this dispatch.

criteria_coverage.criterion: An authenticated user can post a comment on a resource; unauthenticated requests are rejected with 401.
tests: comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: POST > returns 401 when unauthenticated (also asserts createComment not called)
comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: POST > returns 201 with created Comment on valid input
criteria_coverage.notes: Both directions covered. The 401 test also asserts the service was not invoked, which defends against a route that authorises after doing work.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Body is plain text, trimmed, non-empty after trimming, and <= 2000 chars; violations rejected with 400 + human-readable error.
tests: service.test.ts :: body validation > empty string / whitespace-only / 2001 chars / exactly 2000 / valid body
comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: POST > returns 400 with empty body, returns 400 with body > 2000 chars
gaps: No assertion anywhere that the persisted/returned body is actually TRIMMED. service.test.ts passes '  Great resource!  ' but only asserts `result` is defined — mockInsertReturning returns a canned row, so the value handed to db.insert().values() is never inspected. An implementation that stores the untrimmed string passes.
Boundary at exactly 2000 is asserted only as `resolves.not.toBeUndefined()`; combined with the canned insert mock this is a weak assertion but does correctly distinguish throw vs no-throw.
No route-level test for a malformed/missing JSON payload (e.g. `{}` or non-JSON) — the contract's 400 surface for that shape is untested.
No service-level test that editComment applies the same validation (contract requires it); the 400-on-edit route test drives it entirely from a mocked rejection.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Comments for a resource are readable by anyone who can view the resource (auth required per Ambiguity C).
tests: comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: GET > returns 401 when unauthenticated
comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: GET > returns 200 with paginated CommentWithReplies when authenticated

criteria_coverage.criterion: Listing endpoint returns a paginated response, default page size 20, documented ordering (chronological, oldest first at top level).
tests: comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: GET > passes default limit of 20 and accepts cursor param
gaps: CRITICAL: `listComments` has NO unit tests at all. service.test.ts imports createComment, createReply, editComment, softDeleteComment and both notification functions — listComments is never imported or exercised.
Ordering (created_at ASC, id ASC) is asserted nowhere, at any level. A newest-first or unordered implementation passes the whole suite.
The 'default limit of 20' assertion is guarded by `if (callArgs.limit !== undefined)` — it passes vacuously when the route omits `limit` entirely, which is exactly the bug it is meant to catch.
Cursor semantics (opaque base64 `<iso-created_at>|<id>`, nextCursor null on last page, nextCursor non-null when more pages exist) are never tested. The 200 test uses `nextCursor: null` from a mock.
Contract's limit clamping to [1, 100] is untested — `?limit=0`, `?limit=9999`, `?limit=abc` all unexercised.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Replies are returned nested under their parent so the client can render threading without N+1 round-trips.
tests: comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: GET > returns 200 ... expects body.items[0] toHaveProperty('replies')
gaps: The only 'replies' assertion checks a property on a hand-written mock fixture that the test itself supplies to `mockListComments`. It verifies JSON pass-through, not nesting. `replies: []` in the fixture means even the non-empty case is unexercised.

No service-level test that replies are grouped under the correct parent, that `replies` is non-null/empty-array when there are none, that replies are ordered oldest-first, or that replies never leak into `items` at the top level (a contract invariant).

criteria_coverage.criterion: An authenticated user can reply to any existing (non-deleted) top-level comment.
tests: replies/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 201 with created reply Comment (asserts parentId, body, authorId)
replies/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 401 when unauthenticated
gaps: No service-level happy path for `createReply`. There is no test that a valid top-level parent produces an insert with `parent_id = parentId`. The 201 route test asserts against a fixture returned by a mocked `createReply`, so the actual parent linkage is never verified.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Threading is strictly one level: replying to a reply returns 400.
tests: service.test.ts :: createReply — threading enforcement > throws ValidationError with 'cannot reply to a reply' when the parent is itself a reply
replies/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 400 when attempting to reply to a reply (asserts error message contains 'cannot reply to a reply')
criteria_coverage.notes: This is the best-covered rule in the suite. The service test drives the real enforcement (parent row with non-null parentId) and asserts both the error class and the message; the route test independently pins the ValidationError -> 400 mapping. Message-text coupling between the two layers is intentional and correct here.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Replies to a comment are ordered chronologically, oldest first.
gaps: Untested. Falls entirely inside the untested `listComments`. Related ticket edge case 'concurrent replies ... stable ordering, no reordering on refresh' is also untested.

criteria_coverage.criterion: A comment's author can edit the body of their own comment; edits subject to the same validation as new comments.
tests: comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: PATCH > returns 200 with updated Comment
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: PATCH > returns 400 with empty body
gaps: No service-level happy path for `editComment` (author edits successfully). service.test.ts covers only the AuthzError branch.

No service-level test that `editComment` validates the body (empty / >2000). The route-level 400 comes from a mocked rejection, so an implementation of editComment that skips validation entirely still passes.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Edited comments are visibly marked as edited in listings (edited indicator + edit timestamp).
tests: comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: PATCH > returns 200 ... expect(responseBody.editedAt).not.toBeNull()
gaps: The `editedAt` assertion reads a value the test itself hard-coded into `mockEditComment.mockResolvedValue`. It is tautological — it cannot fail regardless of implementation.
No service-level test that `editComment` actually sets `editedAt` (e.g. asserting the object passed to `db.update().set()` contains editedAt/updatedAt).
The 'visibly marked' half of the criterion is a UI concern and there are no component tests in the repo at all (no tests under src/components or src/app/resources).

criteria_coverage.criterion: A comment's author can delete their own comment.
tests: service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > allows the comment author to delete their own comment
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: DELETE > returns 204 on success (author can delete their own)

criteria_coverage.criterion: A resource owner can delete any comment on their own resource.
tests: service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > allows the resource owner to delete any comment on their resource
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: DELETE > returns 204 when resource owner deletes
criteria_coverage.notes: The route test asserts `softDeleteComment` was called with the owner's actorId, but does not assert `resourceOwnerId` was correctly resolved and passed through. A route that passes a wrong/undefined resourceOwnerId would still pass.

criteria_coverage.criterion: A user with the `moderator` role can delete any comment on any resource.
tests: service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > allows a moderator to delete any comment regardless of ownership
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: DELETE > returns 204 when moderator deletes (asserts actorRole: 'moderator' is forwarded)
gaps: The `admin` role is in the contract's authorised set but is never exercised.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Deletion is a SOFT delete: record retained, excluded from normal listings, replaced by 'This comment has been deleted' placeholder so thread structure and reply anchors are preserved.
tests: service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > calls db.update (not db.delete) to set deletedAt
gaps: CRITICAL: the placeholder half is completely untested. The contract states a soft-deleted top-level comment must surface with `body = "This comment has been deleted"`, `authorId = null`, `authorName = null`, and that the original body/author is never exposed. That redaction lives in `listComments`, which has zero tests. A leak of the original body or author identity — a privacy defect — would not be caught.
The passing test asserts `mockDbUpdate` was called and `mockDbDelete` was not, but never inspects the `set()` payload, so it does not verify `deletedAt` is actually assigned.
Thread continuity (replies remain visible under a soft-deleted parent — an explicit ticket edge case) is untested; again inside `listComments`.

'Excluded from normal listings' as it applies to soft-deleted REPLIES vs top-level comments is untested (contract says replies are returned regardless of deleted_at state — an easy place for an implementation to diverge silently).

criteria_coverage.criterion: Editing or deleting a comment you do not own (and are not authorised to moderate) returns 403.
tests: service.test.ts :: editComment — authorization > throws AuthzError when the editor is not the comment author
service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > throws AuthzError for a stranger (unrelated user, role=user)
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: PATCH > returns 403 when editor is not the author
comments/[commentId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: DELETE > returns 403 when actor not authorized
criteria_coverage.notes: Correctly layered: the service tests drive real authorisation logic against a realistic joined row; the route tests pin the AuthzError -> 403 mapping. This is the pattern the rest of the suite should follow.
gaps: Contract says resource owners and moderators may NOT edit (only delete). There is no test that a moderator or resource owner attempting PATCH is rejected — a privilege-escalation gap where an over-permissive implementation passes.

criteria_coverage.criterion: When a comment is posted, the resource owner receives an in-app notification — unless the commenter is the resource owner.
tests: service.test.ts :: notification self-suppression > createNotificationForComment does NOT insert when actorId === resourceOwnerId
comments/__tests__/route.test.ts :: POST > fires notification (fire-and-forget)
gaps: CRITICAL / VACUOUS-PASS: the suppression rule is tested only in the negative. There is no test asserting that `createNotificationForComment` DOES insert a row when `actorId !== resourceOwnerId`. An implementation whose body is `return;` — never notifying anyone — passes every notification test in this suite. This is precisely the 'tests pass but test the wrong thing' failure mode.
The inserted row's contents (recipientId = resourceOwnerId, type = 'comment_on_resource', resourceId, commentId, readAt = null) are asserted nowhere.

The route-level 'fires notification' test asserts `resourceId`, `commentId`, `actorId` were forwarded, but NOT `resourceOwnerId` — the one field the suppression rule depends on. If the route resolves the owner incorrectly (or passes undefined), the test still passes and suppression silently breaks.

The contract requires notification failure to not fail the 201. There is no test where `createNotificationForComment` rejects and the response is still 201 — a rejected fire-and-forget promise could plausibly surface as a 500 or an unhandled rejection.

criteria_coverage.criterion: When a reply is posted, the parent comment's author receives a notification — unless the replier is the parent comment author.
tests: service.test.ts :: notification self-suppression > createNotificationForReply does NOT insert when actorId === parentCommentAuthorId
replies/__tests__/route.test.ts :: returns 201 ... expect(mockCreateNotificationForReply).toHaveBeenCalled()
gaps: Same vacuous-pass defect as AC-N1: no positive-path insert test. A no-op implementation passes.

The route test asserts only `toHaveBeenCalled()` with no argument matcher — `parentCommentAuthorId` is never checked, so the route could pass the replier's own id (which would suppress every notification) or `undefined` and still pass.

The route fixture resolves the parent author via a DB mock (`{ authorId: PARENT_AUTHOR_ID }`) but never asserts that value reached the notification call — the wiring the whole rule depends on is unverified.
No route-level test for the self-reply case (replier === parent author) end-to-end.

criteria_coverage.criterion: A user can list their unread notifications and mark an individual notification as read.
tests: notifications/__tests__/route.test.ts :: GET > returns 401 / returns 200 with unread notifications only / excludes already-read notifications
notifications/[notificationId]/__tests__/route.test.ts :: PATCH > returns 401 / 403 when recipient is different user / 200 with readAt set
gaps: `excludes already-read notifications (readAt not null)` is fully vacuous: the mock is configured to return only unread rows and the test then asserts no read rows came back. Its own inline comment concedes this ('The query filters for readAt IS NULL, so mock returns only unread'). It cannot fail. If the route drops the isNull filter, this test still passes.
`returns 200 with unread notifications only` has the same defect — it asserts `readAt === null` on rows the test itself supplied.
Scoping to the CURRENT USER is untested for GET. A route that returns every user's notifications passes — a data-leak class defect.
Ordering `createdAt DESC` is untested (single-row fixture).
PATCH 200 asserts `readAt` is non-null from a canned update mock; it never asserts the route actually set readAt (no inspection of the `set()` payload). A PATCH that updates nothing passes.
PATCH 404 (notification not found) is in the contract's response table but has no test.
GOOD: the PATCH 403 test is genuine — the route's own recipient check runs against a mock row with a foreign recipientId and the 403 is produced by real logic.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Notifications include enough context to link back to the originating resource + comment.
gaps: Fixtures include `resourceId` and `commentId`, but no test asserts their presence or correctness in any response. GET /api/notifications only asserts `items` is an array of length 1 and `readAt === null`.
No test that the notification row written by the service carries the triggering resourceId/commentId (part of the missing positive-path notification tests).

criteria_coverage.criterion: Deleting the source comment does not retroactively send a 'new comment' notification; existing notifications handle the deleted target gracefully (no 500).
gaps: Entirely untested. No test asserts DELETE does not create notifications, and none covers opening/reading a notification whose target comment or resource has been deleted.

criteria_coverage.criterion: All comment/reply/notification write endpoints require authentication.
tests: POST /comments 401
PATCH /comments/[commentId] 401
DELETE /comments/[commentId] 401
POST /comments/[commentId]/replies 401
PATCH /notifications/[notificationId] 401
GET /comments 401
GET /notifications 401
criteria_coverage.notes: All seven HTTP surfaces in the contract have a 401 test, and every write-endpoint 401 test additionally asserts the downstream service was not invoked. This is the strongest column in the matrix.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Endpoints are covered by automated tests (Vitest).
criteria_coverage.notes: All 7 contract endpoints have a Vitest file. Coverage exists; depth is the problem addressed by the findings above.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Fetching the comment count for a resource does not require scanning all comment rows.
gaps: No comment-count surface is exercised anywhere in the suite. This may be out of the contract's scope (the contract defines no count endpoint or function), in which case it should be explicitly deferred rather than silently dropped.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Comment bodies are plain text; the client must render them without HTML interpretation (no XSS via comment content).
gaps: No test posts a body containing HTML/script markup and asserts it round-trips as inert text. No component tests exist in the repo at all, so the rendering half cannot be covered by the current suite.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Comment UI renders RTL text correctly; composer and thread controls are keyboard-navigable and screen-reader labelled. Threading visually represented; stable chronological display.
gaps: There are zero UI/component tests in the repository (only the 7 files under review plus pre-existing repo-hygiene and /api/health tests). All UI-level acceptance criteria are unverified.

criteria_coverage.criterion: Contract: getCurrentUser returns CurrentUser for the dev user, null for no session, honours the x-test-user injection header, never rejects; id is always a non-empty UUID and role is one of user/moderator/admin.
tests: auth.test.ts :: without x-test-user header > DEV_USER_ID honoured / fixed-UUID fallback / never rejects
auth.test.ts :: with x-test-user header > valid JSON CurrentUser / 'null' string / invalid JSON
auth.test.ts :: returned user shape invariants > id UUID / name string / role enum
criteria_coverage.notes: Env-var tests correctly save and restore process.env.DEV_USER_ID in a finally block, so they do not leak state into sibling tests. The test seam this file validates is what every route test's 401 case depends on.

test_findings.title: listComments is entirely untested
test_findings.detail: The service test file imports createComment, createReply, editComment, softDeleteComment, createNotificationForComment and createNotificationForReply — but never listComments. This one omission leaves the majority of the read-path contract unverified: ordering (created_at ASC, id ASC), reply nesting and reply ordering, the `replies` non-null invariant, the 'no replies at top level' invariant, cursor encode/decode, nextCursor null-on-last-page, the default limit of 20, and — most seriously — the soft-delete redaction (body -> 'This comment has been deleted', authorId -> null, authorName -> null, original body/author never exposed).
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: An implementation that returns comments newest-first, flattens replies to the top level, leaks the original body and author of a deleted comment, ignores the cursor, or drops replies of a deleted parent would pass 100% of the current suite.
test_findings.recommendation: Add a `describe('listComments')` block to service.test.ts driving the existing db mock: (a) a soft-deleted top-level row asserts body === 'This comment has been deleted' AND authorId === null AND authorName === null AND that the original body string appears nowhere in the serialised result; (b) replies grouped under the right parent, ordered oldest-first, and absent from `items`; (c) a page at the limit returns a non-null nextCursor and the next call with that cursor returns the following rows; (d) replies of a soft-deleted parent are still returned.

test_findings.title: Notification suppression is tested only negatively — a no-op implementation passes
test_findings.detail: Both tests in the 'notification self-suppression' block assert `expect(mockDbInsert).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`. There is no counterpart asserting an insert DOES happen when actorId !== recipient, and no assertion on the inserted row's shape.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: `export async function createNotificationForComment() { return; }` and `createNotificationForReply() { return; }` — implementations that never notify anyone — satisfy every notification test in the suite, at both service and route level. The entire notifications feature could be absent and the suite would be green. This is the canonical 'passing tests that test the wrong thing'.
test_findings.recommendation: For each function add a positive test with distinct actor/recipient ids asserting `mockDbInsert` was called once AND `mockInsertValues` received an object matching { recipientId: <owner|parentAuthor>, type: 'comment_on_resource' | 'reply_to_comment', resourceId, commentId, readAt: null }. Without this the negative tests carry no signal.

test_findings.title: The notification wiring test omits the one field suppression depends on
test_findings.detail: The `expect.objectContaining` matcher checks resourceId, commentId and actorId — but not `resourceOwnerId`. The DB mock resolves `[{ ownerId: OWNER_ID }]`, yet no assertion confirms OWNER_ID reached the notification call. Same class of defect, worse, in replies/route.test.ts:172 which asserts only bare `toHaveBeenCalled()` with no argument matcher at all, leaving `parentCommentAuthorId` unchecked despite the DB mock supplying PARENT_AUTHOR_ID.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: A route that passes `resourceOwnerId: undefined`, or that mistakenly passes the actor's own id as the recipient (which would suppress every notification, or address it to the wrong user), passes both tests.
test_findings.recommendation: Extend the matchers to `{ resourceId, commentId, actorId: USER_ID, resourceOwnerId: OWNER_ID }` and `{ resourceId, replyCommentId, actorId: USER_ID, parentCommentAuthorId: PARENT_AUTHOR_ID }`. Add a route-level self-notification case: current user === OWNER_ID / === PARENT_AUTHOR_ID, still expecting 201.

test_findings.title: Both GET /api/notifications assertions are tautological; user-scoping is untested
test_findings.detail: `excludes already-read notifications` configures the mock to return only unread rows and then asserts no read rows were returned; its own comment admits the mock is doing the filtering. `returns 200 with unread notifications only` asserts readAt === null on the same test-supplied fixture. Neither test can fail. Separately, nothing asserts the query is scoped to the current user, and the `createdAt DESC` ordering is untested against a one-row fixture.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: Dropping the `isNull(readAt)` predicate, dropping the `eq(recipientId, currentUser.id)` predicate (a cross-user data leak), or ordering ascending all pass.
test_findings.recommendation: Assert on the query arguments rather than on the returned fixture: capture the `where(...)` argument and assert it composes an isNull(readAt) with an eq(recipientId, USER_ID), and that `orderBy` received a desc(createdAt). Alternatively feed a mixed read/unread, multi-user, out-of-order fixture — but only if the route filters/sorts in application code. Also assert items carry resourceId and commentId (AC-N4).

test_findings.title: Conditional assertion makes the 'default limit 20' test unfailable
test_findings.detail: `if (callArgs.limit !== undefined) { expect(callArgs.limit).toBe(20); }` — when the route forgets to pass a limit, `callArgs.limit` is undefined, the branch is skipped, and the test passes. The guard disables the test in exactly the scenario it exists to detect.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: A route that never forwards `limit` (so the default is silently whatever the service chooses, or nothing) passes.
test_findings.recommendation: Remove the conditional. Either assert `limit` is 20/undefined-with-a-documented-service-default unconditionally, or split into two explicit tests: no `?limit` -> service receives 20 (or the route documents delegation and the service test pins the default); `?limit=500` -> service receives 100 (clamp upper); `?limit=0` -> receives 1 (clamp lower); `?limit=abc` -> receives 20.

test_findings.title: Mutation payloads are never inspected — trimming, editedAt and deletedAt are unverified
test_findings.detail: Across createComment, editComment and softDeleteComment the tests assert only that the right chain method was reached (`mockDbUpdate` called, `mockDbDelete` not called) or that the promise resolved. `mockInsertValues` and the update `set()` argument are never asserted against. Consequently: body trimming is unverified (AC-P2), `editedAt`/`updatedAt` being set on edit is unverified (AC-E2), and `deletedAt` being set on soft delete is unverified (AC-E6).
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: `softDeleteComment` calling `db.update(...).set({}).where(...)` — updating nothing — passes 'calls db.update (not db.delete) to set deletedAt' despite the comment being deleted only in name. Likewise `editComment` that updates body but never sets editedAt passes, so 'edited' would never render.
test_findings.recommendation: Assert on payloads: `expect(mockInsertValues).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ body: 'Great resource!', parentId: null }))` for the trim case; capture the `set()` argument (expose mockUpdateSet from the hoisted block — it is currently created but not returned) and assert it contains deletedAt / editedAt.

test_findings.title: Missing happy paths for createReply and editComment; missing negative paths for editComment validation
test_findings.detail: `createReply` is tested only for its two failure branches (reply-to-reply, deleted parent) — never for the success case that a valid top-level parent yields an insert with parent_id = parentId. `editComment` is tested only for AuthzError — never for a successful author edit, and never for body validation despite the contract requiring the same rules as createComment. `createReply` body validation is likewise untested at the service level.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: A `createReply` that inserts with `parent_id = null` (silently creating a top-level comment instead of a reply) passes. An `editComment` that accepts a 5000-character or empty body passes.
test_findings.recommendation: Add: createReply success -> mockInsertValues receives parentId; createReply with '' and 'a'.repeat(2001) -> ValidationError; createReply NotFoundError when the parent lookup returns []; editComment success by the author -> resolves with updated body; editComment with an invalid body -> ValidationError.

test_findings.title: No test that moderators / resource owners are blocked from EDITING
test_findings.detail: The contract is explicit: 'Resource-owner and moderator roles may NOT edit — only delete.' No test exercises PATCH as moderatorUser or ownerUser. Both fixtures already exist in the file and are used only by the DELETE block.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: An implementation that reuses the delete authorisation matrix for edits — letting a moderator rewrite another teacher's words — passes the entire suite. This is a privilege-escalation and content-integrity defect.
test_findings.recommendation: Add PATCH-as-moderator and PATCH-as-resource-owner cases expecting 403, and a corresponding service-level editComment test where actorRole is 'moderator' but editorId !== authorId, expecting AuthzError.

test_findings.title: 204 responses are not asserted to have an empty body, and 404 mappings are untested
test_findings.detail: The three DELETE tests correctly assert status 204 (per resolved-ambiguity #3, and not 200 — good), but none asserts the body is empty, which is the defining property of 204. `NotFoundError` is imported in this file but never used: neither PATCH 404 nor DELETE 404 is tested, despite both appearing in the contract's response tables. The same unused-import pattern means the 404 branch is dead spec here.
test_findings.recommendation: Add `expect(await response.text()).toBe('')` to one 204 test. Add PATCH-404 and DELETE-404 cases driven by a mocked NotFoundError rejection (mirroring the pattern already used in replies/route.test.ts).

test_findings.title: '404 when parent soft-deleted' and '404 when parent not found' are the same test
test_findings.detail: Both configure `mockCreateReply.mockRejectedValue(new NotFoundError('Not found'))` and assert 404. They are byte-identical in behaviour, differing only in the request body string and the test name. They give a false impression that two distinct conditions are covered; the soft-deleted-parent distinction is only genuinely covered in service.test.ts (which does test it properly).
test_findings.recommendation: Keep one route-level NotFoundError -> 404 mapping test. If both scenarios should be distinguished, they must be distinguished where the branch actually lives (the service), which already has the soft-deleted case — add the 'parent row absent' service case alongside it.

test_findings.title: No 500 / error-propagation coverage; notification failure must not fail the write
test_findings.detail: Every contract endpoint documents a 500 response; none is tested. More importantly the contract states notification dispatch is fire-and-forget and 'its failure must not fail the 201 response', and that is untested for both POST /comments and POST .../replies.
test_findings.if_impl_were_buggy: An awaited notification call that rejects would turn a successful comment into a 500 — or produce an unhandled promise rejection — undetected.
test_findings.recommendation: Add: service throws a generic Error -> route returns 500 with an { error } body; `createNotificationForComment` rejects -> POST still returns 201 and no unhandled rejection is raised.

test_findings.title: 'returns null when x-test-user is invalid JSON' — the TEST is correct; the failure is a code bug
test_findings.detail: Reviewed against the contract without opening src/lib/auth.ts. The contract states the x-test-user header is a 'JSON-encoded CurrentUser | null [that] overrides the return value for test injection'. It does not spell out the malformed-JSON case, so this is strictly a contract gap — but the test's chosen reading (malformed -> null) is the only defensible one: an unparseable auth-override header must never resolve to an authenticated principal, and falling back to the dev user turns a garbled header into a silent authentication. Every 401 test in the other six files depends on this seam behaving predictably.
test_findings.verdict_on_test: Test is correct as written. Do NOT weaken or delete it to make the suite green. Fix the implementation to return null on JSON.parse failure, and consider adding the malformed-header case explicitly to the contract's getCurrentUser semantics.

test_findings.title: Route tests mock the service, so they verify wiring and status mapping only — which makes service-level gaps load-bearing
test_findings.detail: This is a legitimate and well-executed layering choice: every route test stubs @/lib/comments/service and asserts (a) auth gating, (b) error-class -> status-code mapping, (c) argument forwarding. The consequence is that ALL behavioural verification must live in service.test.ts. Because service.test.ts omits listComments entirely (F1), omits positive notification paths (F2), and never inspects mutation payloads (F6), those behaviours have no home in the suite at all. The layering is not the problem; the unfilled lower layer is.

test_findings.title: No component/UI tests exist, so all presentational acceptance criteria are unverified
test_findings.detail: The repository contains only the seven files under review plus pre-existing repo-hygiene and /api/health tests. Criteria depending on rendering — the 'edited' indicator being visible, threading being visually represented, comment bodies rendering without HTML interpretation (XSS), RTL correctness, keyboard navigability and screen-reader labelling — have no coverage.
test_findings.recommendation: Either add component tests for the comment thread and composer, or have the orchestrator explicitly record these criteria as deferred so they are not mistaken for covered.

unmapped_tests.test: auth.test.ts :: without x-test-user header > returns the dev user when DEV_USER_ID env var is set / falls back to the fixed UUID / never rejects
unmapped_tests.rationale: Maps to the contract's getCurrentUser semantics rather than to a product acceptance criterion. This is scaffolding for the auth prerequisite (issue #2) that the ticket explicitly assumes; the test seam it validates underpins every 401 test in the suite. Justified.

unmapped_tests.test: auth.test.ts :: returned user shape invariants > id is a UUID / name is a string / role is one of user|moderator|admin
unmapped_tests.rationale: Contract invariants. `role` in particular is a real precondition for the moderator authorisation path (AC-E5).

unmapped_tests.test: service.test.ts :: softDeleteComment > calls db.update (not db.delete) to set deletedAt
unmapped_tests.rationale: Maps to AC-E6. The 'not db.delete' half is a genuine and valuable guard against a hard delete; the 'sets deletedAt' half is asserted only in the test's name (see F6).

strengths: Auth gating is comprehensive: all 7 contract endpoints have a 401 test, and every write endpoint additionally asserts the service was not invoked.

One-level threading (the subtlest business rule) is properly covered at BOTH layers — real enforcement in service.test.ts against a parent row with a non-null parentId, plus the 400 mapping and error text at the route.
The softDeleteComment authorisation matrix is genuinely exercised (author / resource owner / moderator allowed, stranger rejected) with real logic, not mocks.
DELETE correctly asserts 204 rather than 200, matching resolved ambiguity #3.
PATCH /api/notifications/[id] 403 is a real test — the route's own recipient check produces the status from a foreign-recipient fixture.
The 'not db.delete' assertion is a well-chosen guard against a hard delete regression.
auth.test.ts restores process.env.DEV_USER_ID in finally blocks, avoiding cross-test state leakage.
blocking_changes_required: F1 — add listComments unit tests (ordering, reply nesting, cursor/nextCursor, and above all the soft-delete placeholder + author redaction).
F2 — add positive-path notification tests asserting an insert occurs with the correct row shape when actor !== recipient. Without these the entire notifications feature is vacuously green.
F3 — assert resourceOwnerId / parentCommentAuthorId are forwarded to the notification calls at the route layer.
one_line_summary: Auth gating, the one-level threading rule and the soft-delete authorisation matrix are genuinely well covered, but the suite has three blocking holes — listComments is entirely untested (so the 'This comment has been deleted' placeholder, author redaction, ordering, reply nesting and pagination are all unverified), notification suppression is tested only in the negative so a no-op notifier passes everything, and several assertions (default limit 20, unread-only filtering, editedAt) are tautological or self-disabling; separately the known auth.ts malformed-JSON failure is a code bug and the test asserting null must not be weakened.
